member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Telemetry.ForzaLayout
member.summary: The three "Data Out" packet layouts Forza titles emit, all understood by SimHub and most dashboards. Receivers validate by exact length.

remarks.para: is the Motorsport 7 "sled" (physics only). appends the 79-byte dash block directly at 232. inserts 12 unknown bytes at 232, then the dash at 244, then one trailing byte — 324 in total. The intuitive 323 is rejected silently: SimHub logs "started receiving unprocessed data" at packet rate and never connects (measured, milestone-wheel-tools, 2026-08-30).
OutRun2006Tweaks-FFB emits ; art-of-sim-rally, iracing-arcade-wheel and cruisn-collection emit . The two are not interchangeable: a dash profile expects one or the other.

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Telemetry.ForzaPacket
member.summary: Writes the 324-byte Forza Horizon 4/5 "Data Out" UDP packet.

remarks.para: Emitting a format consumers already understand is the whole point: SimHub, dashboards, motion rigs and bass shakers all speak Forza Data Out, so art of rally gains that entire ecosystem without anyone writing a plugin for it.

The layout is the Forza Motorsport 7 "sled" (232 bytes) followed by a 12-byte block the Horizon titles insert, then the "dash" fields. That 12-byte insert is the whole reason FM7 dash offsets do not work here and why the packet is 324 rather than 311 bytes.

Offsets are not guesses. Speed at 256 and Gear at 319 are the two that pin the layout, and both are copied from a harness in the sibling cruisn-collection project that was validated live against SimHub's Forza Horizon profile. Everything else follows from field order and sizes. See docs/TELEMETRY.md.
All fields are little-endian, matching x86/x64 hosts. Unwritten bytes stay zero, which consumers read as "not supported" rather than as bad data.

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Telemetry.IdleKeeper
member.summary: Keeps a dashboard alive while no game is driving: emits zeroed frames at a low rate so gauges rest at zero instead of freezing on the last value.

remarks.para: SimHub and most dash software hold the last received values when a stream stops, so a game that exits (or crashes) leaves the dash stuck. Lifted from cruisn-collection's ForzaKeeper (2026-08), which learned two things the hard way, both encoded here:

list.item: The keeper frame must carry the same engine constants as the game's frames. A fully zero packet (EngineMaxRpm = 0) is degenerate and can wedge SimHub's normalisation state so it ignores the real stream afterwards.
Gear is 1, because 0 renders as reverse and Forza has no code for neutral.

remarks.para: ('K') is stamped into the unused trailing byte of the Horizon layout so a probe can tell keeper frames from game frames. The keeper is inert while is set.

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Telemetry.RpmSynthesizer
member.summary: A plausible engine speed for games that have none, from road speed and a gear-ratio table. Three projects had each written their own version of this (OutRun 2006, Cruis'n, Gravel); this is the one to keep.

remarks.para: The output exists to drive rev counters, shift lights and bass shakers, not to be true. It rises through each gear's speed band from idle to just under the redline, drops on the up-shift, and never exceeds . When the game reports no gear either, the gear is inferred from speed against the same table.
Pass the frame's EngineMaxRpm/EngineIdleRpm the same values every frame — dashboards normalise against them, and the idle keeper must use the same constants (see ).

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Telemetry.TelemetryFrame
member.summary: One physics-frame snapshot, in neutral units, ready to be encoded.

remarks.para: Deliberately independent of both art of rally and Forza. The mod fills this from the game's CarController/Drivetrain/Wheel objects, and encodes it. Keeping the middle layer neutral is what lets the encoder be unit-tested without Unity present, and what would let a second output format be added without touching the game-reading code.

Units follow Forza's conventions so the encoder stays a pure memcpy with no hidden arithmetic: metres, metres/second, radians, watts, newton-metres. The conversions from art of rally's units live in the mod, documented in docs/TELEMETRY.md.

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Telemetry.TelemetrySender
member.summary: Fire-and-forget UDP sender for frames.

remarks.para: Uses a reusable serialization buffer and contains network exceptions. Send is synchronous: callers with a strict physics deadline should invoke it from a bounded latest-sample worker rather than assume a nonblocking send. UDP callers must tolerate dropped packets.
Not thread-safe: the shared scratch buffer assumes a single caller. That matches how it is used (one Unity FixedUpdate), and a lock on the hot path would cost more than it protects.
